items.title: Jimmy Heath interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, September 8, 2014
items.q: Bony James. They listen to that and they know that those people can get over.

ctx.x: How do you tell an 18-year-old college freshman how to put more soul — because I’ve got this problem where I teach.

They’re listening — and they’re listening to too much soul sometimes you know. People who don’t really play with a lot of science, the popular ones — Kenny G — they listen to that. Bony James. They listen to that and they know that those people can get over. So they give up. They have what they want to do, their expression, to please an audience. That’s a different thing. If you can keep your idea of what music should be like and still get over, that’s when you’ve reached a very happy compromise with an audience.…
Well said. I’ve had a debate sometimes with musicians about, are there wrong notes when you improvise?
